decision: Outcome sampling: uniform (every prompt × every outcome) rather than stratified weights
rationale: Preregistration §3 internally inconsistent: count of 1200 = 300×4 implies uniform, but stratification table specifies weighted. Uniform gives ≥300 trajectories per (tool×outcome) cell — necessary for within-error-type probe (G-WITHIN, gate threshold 50% on ≥2 of 3 errors). Stratified would give 10–50 trajectories per cell, insufficient for the gate.
outcome: Documented in prereg_vs_final.md; uniform sampling adopted for all main runs.
alternative: Re-do with stratified weights — rejected: insufficient power for G-WITHIN.

decision: Qwen3-8B shows near-zero give-up rate on error trajectories (~2%), while Hermes-3 shows ~45%
rationale: Qwen3-8B rate_limited and invalid_arg outcomes yield 0 give-up trajectories; only no_results yields ~14. This falls below the 60-sample minimum for 3-way probe training. Behavioral hypothesis: Qwen3-8B is optimized for resilient tool use and rarely emits final_answer after errors. This is itself a publishable cross-model finding. Resolution: add 2-class probe fallback (retry vs non-retry) when give-up count < 20; run it as a secondary analysis and report the cross-model behavioral difference in the paper.
outcome: Adding 2-class fallback probe path to run_analysis.py; also logging give-up rate per outcome as supplementary finding.
alternative: Re-tune system prompt to increase Qwen give-up rate — rejected because (a) it would change the experimental protocol post-hoc and (b) the natural difference between models is itself scientifically informative.
